messages:
Sofia: quick thread — VerveLens case study + bench note. publish target = Wed next week 9am PT. Need: recorded interview, approved quote, a short benchmark methodology blurb (to avoid misinterpretation), two social cards, and webinar CTA. who can lead the production ops?

Raj: I can run ops. booked VerveLens interview Fri 2pm PT (30m). prefer audio + transcript + one short clip for social. I'll add recorder link to the checklist.

Mei: I'll draft the hero quote and write the benchmark blurb. Important: VerveLens asked us to include methodology + dataset notes so results are reproducible.

Tom: Metrics from telemetry: p95 latency down from 340ms to 110ms (~3.1x); steady-state serving cost = 26% lower. Also have an A/B where caching reduced token cost by another ~8% under steady prefixes. sheet: <https://docs.redwood/internal/vervelens-metrics-2498>.

Sofia: nice. For the bench blurb let's be explicit: dataset size, sequence lengths, and any prompt engineering. Legal prefers conservative phrasing on comparisons.

Mei: draft benchmark blurb (working): "Benchmark methodology: VerveLens traffic profile (median seq 128 tokens) was replayed against baseline infra. Measurements capture p95 latency and per-token serving cost over 24h steady-state traffic. Results reflect Redwood's default KV caching + batching config. Individual results may vary based on workload."

Raj: adding checklist & recorder: <https://drive.redwood/internal/checklists/vervelens-2498>. recorder link + CMS draft in folder.

Tom: note on A/B: the test that applied prefix caching showed 8% additional token cost savings on long-running sessions; include as a sidebar item, not headline.

Sofia: agreed — sidebar only. Mei, draft hero + one-sentence customer pull. keep numbers but avoid comparative model names.

Mei: hero draft: "VerveLens reduced p95 latency ~3.1x and cut serving costs by 26% with Redwood, enabling faster iteration on recommendation models." one-sentence pull: "Redwood's caching and routing let us ship new personalization features without blowing up infra spend."

LegalBot: please submit quote & metrics language via approval form: <https://legal.redwood/submit?case=vervelens-2498>. Legal will check name usage, percentage claims, and benchmarking wording. ETA 24-48h.

Sofia: customer consent? Raj, did VerveLens sign the release?

Raj: consent uploaded to the approval form and project folder: <https://drive.redwood/content/vervelens-consent.pdf>.

Mei: drafted a short customer quote pulled from transcript: "Switching to Redwood let us reduce tail latency and control serving costs so we could iterate faster." submitting to LegalBot.

LegalBot: initial review: please replace vague phrases like "tail latency" with specific metrics (e.g., p95) and avoid words like "control" in a way that could imply vendor lock. Also request we include the benchmark methodology blurb in the case study for context.

Mei: updated quote: "Redwood reduced our p95 latency by about 3.1x and lowered serving costs by 26%, which helped us accelerate product iteration." resubmitted.

LegalBot: approved with stylistic edits: replace "about 3.1x" -> "about 3x" in headline copy; final approval document uploaded: <https://legal.redwood/approvals/vervelens-2498/approved.pdf>. Please archive the consent and approval.

Sofia: noted. Mei update hero to "about 3x" per legal. Keep the exact 3.1x in the methodology section where we show the table.

Mei: done. hero now: "VerveLens reduced p95 latency by about 3x and reduced serving costs by 26% with Redwood." methodology section contains the full numbers and A/B sidebar.

Tom: Sales routing: add UTMs and tags: utm_campaign=vervelens_case&utm_medium=post&utm_source=marketing. Lead source = vervelens_case. Hook AE webhook to #ae-inbox.

SalesOps: HubSpot flow created: vervelens_case_flow. Webhook tested to #ae-inbox. I also set webinar tag "vervelens_webinar" for registrants. Test lead created and validated.

Raj: assets: recording + transcript + one 20s social clip will be uploaded to folder: <https://drive.redwood/content/vervelens-assets>. CMS draft at <https://cms.redwood/drafts/vervelens-2498>.

Mei: social copy idea: "See how VerveLens cut p95 latency ~3x with Redwood 1 read the case study + join our May webinar for a deep-dive." (will swap the 1 to actual register link in final copy).

LegalBot: requested one final edit to social copy: replace "cut" -> "reduced" and remove any shorthand like "~" in headline for social. Social copy approved in the approval doc.

Mei: updated social: "See how VerveLens reduced p95 latency by about 3x with Redwood 1 read the case study + join our May webinar for a deep-dive." final variants uploaded.

Sofia: timeline check: 1) legal approval (done) 2) CMS draft (done) 3) assets uploaded (in progress, Raj will upload clip by EOD) 4) HubSpot flow live (done) 5) schedule Buffer for Wed 9am PT.

Raj: clip + transcript uploaded. CMS scheduled for Wed 09:00 PT pending final QA. Buffer draft queued.

SalesOps: AE webhook will remain active for 72h post publish. I've set a short report to capture demo conversions from vervelens_case_flow.

Mei: final QA pass done. small OG image tweak. All assets in folder: <https://drive.redwood/content/vervelens-final-assets>.

Tom: smoke test on HubSpot flows & webhook OK. sample lead created with UTM and landed in AE queue. Slack ping displays summary + tags properly.

Sofia: great work team. Raj, flip publish at 9am Wed. I'll post a short announce in #general and share the benchmark blurb in the thread. Locking this thread now. :rocket:
